data: SLS Block 1 (with a non-propulsive spacer in place of the upper stage)
Orion + 4-person crew; rendezvous and docking with pathfinder Starship and Blue Moon landers in low Earth orbit

© NASA — Artemis III. Since NASA's 2026-02-27 architecture change, a crewed low-Earth-orbit test before the first landing: Orion rendezvous and (planned) docking with one or both of the commercial landers' pathfinder versions, docked-vehicle and spacesuit tests, about two weeks in space. Crew named 2026-06-09: Randy Bresnik, Luca Parmitano (ESA), Andre Douglas, Frank Rubio. NASA says 2027 (reports range from mid- to late 2027).
NASA adds mission to Artemis lunar program, updates architecture (2026-02-27)
First crewed test of the commercial lunar landers — Orion plans to dock with one or both in Earth orbit

Artemis III no longer lands on the Moon. In February 2026 NASA changed the plan: before risking a landing, a crew will fly Orion in low Earth orbit and rehearse the hardest new step — rendezvous and docking with the commercial landers that will later carry astronauts to the surface. SLS launches Orion with four crew, flying with a spacer in place of its upper stage, since no push towards the Moon is needed. In orbit, Orion plans to meet and dock with pathfinder versions of one or both of SpaceX's Starship lander and Blue Origin's Blue Moon, and the crew test the joined vehicles' life support, communications and propulsion, along with the new AxEMU spacesuits. The flight lasts about two weeks. It plays the part Apollo 9 played in 1969, when the lunar module was flown and docked in Earth orbit before anyone took it to the Moon. Crew, named in June 2026: Randy Bresnik (commander), Luca Parmitano of ESA (pilot), Andre Douglas and Frank Rubio. NASA plans the flight for 2027.
